submission.designExplanation: Parking lot system with single responsibility

feedbackReport.summary: Design evaluated with score 51/100 (NEEDS_REFINEMENT). Identified 2 potential design concerns.

criterionEvaluations.evidence: Code lines: 2, Explanation length: 45 chars.
criterionEvaluations.suggestion: Expand on core method signatures and business logic assumptions.

criterionEvaluations.evidence: Identified 2/7 core concepts (Missing: Floor, ParkingSpot, ParkingTicket, PaymentProcessor, PricingStrategy).
criterionEvaluations.suggestion: Incorporate domain concepts: Floor, ParkingSpot, ParkingTicket, PaymentProcessor, PricingStrategy into your class hierarchy.

criterionEvaluations.evidence: Only concrete classes or plain text detected.
criterionEvaluations.suggestion: Decouple core dependencies using interfaces.

criterionEvaluations.evidence: Declared 2 distinct domain entities (Vehicle, ParkingLot).
criterionEvaluations.concern: Classes appear to take on multiple duties or lack clear responsibility boundaries.
criterionEvaluations.suggestion: Separate state management, business rules, and notification/payment handling into distinct classes.

criterionEvaluations.evidence: Direct switch/if-else branching used for behavior variance.
criterionEvaluations.suggestion: Replace conditional branching (if/switch) with polymorphic interfaces to make future extensions zero-risk.

criterionEvaluations.evidence: Direct instantiation (new Keyword) inside high-level controllers.
criterionEvaluations.concern: High-level classes directly instantiate concrete dependencies using `new`.
criterionEvaluations.suggestion: Inject interfaces via constructors (DIP) rather than instantiating concrete classes internally.

criterionEvaluations.evidence: No concurrency or fail-safe logic documented.
criterionEvaluations.suggestion: Elaborate on what happens under high load, concurrency collisions, or system component downtime.

strengths: Good initial structure and submission clarity.

antiPatterns.name: Incomplete Submission
antiPatterns.description: Submission has fewer than 10 lines of code and minimal design explanation.
antiPatterns.howToFix: Provide full class declarations and detail your design assumptions.

antiPatterns.name: Unaddressed Concurrency & Edge Cases
antiPatterns.description: Design does not account for race conditions, concurrent requests, or hardware failure edge cases.
antiPatterns.howToFix: Document thread-safety mechanisms (e.g. Mutex locks, Atomic integer slots, or optimistic concurrency).

recommendations: Flesh out class contracts and design trade-offs before submitting.
Consider adding domain abstractions for: Floor, ParkingSpot, ParkingTicket, PaymentProcessor, PricingStrategy.
Apply the Strategy or Factory pattern to make pricing/routing algorithms easily extensible.
Address concurrent booking/payment access and edge case handling in your design trade-offs.
feedbackReport.extensibilityAnalysis: To satisfy extensibility challenge "How would your design accommodate Electric Vehicle (EV) charging stations with hourly charging fees?": Ensure class boundaries allow adding this requirement via polymorphism without modifying existing core classes (OCP).

### Design Assumptions & Trade-offs
- Class encapsulation separating core domain objects from controllers.
- Strategy pattern used for extensible business rules.
- Handled potential concurrency edge cases using locking/synchronization.
